axes.evidence: the sealed corpus, for a token OCCURRENCE census only; no activation, no capture, no forward pass
axes.heldout: not applicable: nothing is fitted.  What IS measured out of sample is the segmentation shift -- position agreement 1.0000 on the sealed corpus and 0.1529 on the frozen review prompts, with tokens-per-byte beside it
axes.selection: the 18432 rows kept by: every added/special token and every one of the 256 ByteLevel alphabet tokens (mandatory -- byte_fallback is false and there is no unk, so those 256 are the only reason an arbitrary byte can still be encoded), the transitive merge-tree closure of everything kept, and then the ranking (-census count, parent token id) until the budget is exactly met.  The census sums two streams over the sealed corpus: the donor-mapped ids the captures ran on and this tokenizer's own canonical segmentation of the same text.  With only 4633 observed tokens admitted beyond the mandatory set, the tie-break -- parent id order, which for a BPE table is its merge order and therefore its training-corpus frequency order -- decides most of this table, and that is stated rather than implied
axes.solve: NONE.  The rows are gathered verbatim; the identity gate is torch.equal against the source table's own bytes, not a tolerance.  The merge list is restricted to the closure (a merge survives iff its product and both operands are kept) and the ids are densely remapped, including the TemplateProcessing special-token ids, which carry hard ids a remap that missed them would silently corrupt

axes.evidence: the campaign's 24 captured batches, RE-TOKENIZED into the child's own vocabulary; the parent is run on the injection of that same segmentation, so the two streams are position-aligned over identical text.  No new corpus, no new prompt
axes.selection: no selection: the diagonals that already exist are overwritten in place, so the parameter count, every tensor shape and config.json are unchanged
axes.solve: prior-anchored ridge on the diagonal, closed form.  min_d ||Z diag(d) E^T - N diag(g) E^T||_F^2 + lambda ||d - g||^2 with Z the CHILD's RMS-normalised terminal residual on its OWN segmentation, N the PARENT's on the position-aligned injection of that same segmentation, E the child's tied table and g the parent's gain (also the prior).  Normal equations [(E^T E) o (Z^T Z)] d = [(E^T E) o (Z^T N)] g, one 1024x1024 SPD solve, no K-column target ever formed.  lambda on the internal fit split (wave-18 law), THE LAW a veto on update scale.  Identity gate: at Z = N the solve returns the prior exactly, asserted synthetically every run
